title: The Silk Road
text: The Silk Road was an ancient network of trade routes, formally established during the Han dynasty of China around 130 BCE, that connected China with Central Asia, South Asia, the Middle East, East Africa, and Southern Europe. The name derives from the lucrative silk trade, but other goods traded included spices, glassware, textiles, and precious metals. The Silk Road also facilitated the spread of religions, diseases (including the bubonic plague), and technologies. It operated for over a thousand years, declining only after maritime trade routes were established in the 15th and 16th centuries. The route passed through important cities including Samarkand, Kashgar, and Antioch.
